name: The Teall household — a name from the post office's letter lists
head: teall_wm

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RETURN, NOT AN ARRIVAL. The office's list of letters uncalled-for is a RETURN — its statement of what was still unclaimed on ONE day — and the paper reprinted one return over as many consecutive issues as it took, so the bound is dated by the return of 1 April 1834 and not by the issue it was read in (T-0425). Somebody was writing to this name at Chicago by 1834-04-01 and at no stated time before it; nothing says when they came. The date lines the printings set, and how they were weighed, stand beside this rule in tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py.

lives_at.note: Not attested: a letter list gives a name and no address.

works_at.note: Not attested. No trade is recorded, so there is no premises to seek.

present_on_scene_date.note: THE CORPUS STOPS BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. Nothing after 1834-04-01 follows this person to 1 July 1835 or says they left. `uncertain` rather than dropped — the distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and a finding, not a gap.

persons.name: Wm. Teall

occupation.note: No source records an occupation for this person. A list of uncalled-for letters prints a name and no trade, and this pass will not read one in.

persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Wm. Teall i 1 Lot Has' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 1 April 1834, column 2 — dated 1834-04-01. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

resident_research.evidence_for: Michigan City history records William Teall arriving in 1834, licensed May 13 to vend merchandise, and listed as a Michigan Township resident.
resident_research.evidence_against: The Chicago waiting letter is dated April 1, 1834 and no source directly identifies the Chicago addressee with the Michigan City merchant.
resident_research.summary: Michigan City history records William Teall arriving in 1834, receiving a May 13 license to vend merchandise and appearing among Michigan Township residents. The exact name, target year and Great Lakes geography make a useful candidate for the April 1834 Chicago waiting letter, but no direct source bridges the two records.
resident_research.notes: plausible Great Lakes transit; candidate only

candidates.basis: Exact name, merchant activity and target-year Great Lakes chronology.
conflicts: The Chicago waiting letter is dated April 1, 1834; the Michigan City merchant license is May 13 and no source explicitly identifies the addressee with the merchant.

merge_ruling.for_merge: A terminal l doubled, 'William' and 'Wm.' being the same forename written long and short, and two returns of the same office ten weeks apart. T-0486 found a William Teall of Michigan City arriving in 1834 and licensed to vend merchandise — a real man of the name in the region in the window, which is the strongest external fact either card has.
merge_ruling.against_merge: TWO RETURNS, AND NEITHER SETS BOTH. 'William Teal' is on the return of 28 January 1834 (#c001) and 'Wm. Teall' on the return of 1 April 1834 (#c002), the latter read as 'Wm. Teall i 1 Lot Has' — a line the impression damaged. Neither return carries the other spelling; neither card is an anchor; the corpus sets Teal nine times and Teall three, and no setting of either ties to a Chicago household. T-0486's Michigan City man is evidence about a name, not a bridge to this town, and the ticket itself stopped at candidate_identity. D6.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.
